groups.name: Dativ: dem / der / dem
groups.intro: The dative marks the indirect object and follows certain verbs (helfen, danken, gehören, folgen, antworten) and prepositions (mit, bei, aus, nach, von). Masculine der becomes dem, feminine die becomes der, neuter das becomes dem; plural die becomes den.

items.en: I help the man.
The book belongs to the woman.
items.note: gehören takes the dative; feminine die becomes der.

items.en: We thank the teacher.
items.note: danken takes the dative; masculine der becomes dem.

items.en: She follows the dog.
I live with my parents.
items.note: bei takes the dative; plural die becomes den.

items.p: Mit ___ Auto fahre ich zur Arbeit.
items.en: I drive to work by car.
items.note: mit takes the dative; neuter das becomes dem.

items.en: I have just come from school.
I help a small child.
items.note: Indefinite article in the dative masculine/neuter is einem.

items.en: He answers his colleague.
items.note: antworten takes the dative; feminine die becomes der.

groups.subtitle: The dative case

groups.name: Personalpronomen im Dativ (mir, dir …)
groups.intro: Dative personal pronouns are mir, dir, ihm, ihr, uns, euch, ihnen. They are used with dative verbs like helfen, danken, geben, gefallen, gehören, zeigen.

items.en: Can you help me?
items.note: helfen takes the dative: ich becomes mir.

items.en: I give you the book.
items.note: The receiver is in the dative: du becomes dir.

items.en: We thank him for the help.
She likes the dress very much.
items.note: gefallen takes the dative; dative of sie (sg.) is ihr.

items.en: The teacher explains the grammar to us.
I show you the photos.
I like helping them.
The house belongs to us.
items.note: gehören takes the dative: wir becomes uns.

groups.subtitle: Dative pronouns

groups.name: Wechselpräpositionen (in, an, auf …)
groups.intro: Wechselpräpositionen (in, an, auf, über, unter, vor, hinter, neben, zwischen) take the accusative for direction (Wohin?) and the dative for location (Wo?).

items.en: I go to school.
I am at school.
The book is lying on the table.

items.p: Ich lege das Buch auf ___ Tisch.
items.en: I put the book on the table.
The cat jumps onto the sofa.
items.note: Movement towards something takes the accusative.

items.p: Wir hängen das Bild an ___ Wand.
items.en: We hang the picture on the wall.
The picture hangs on the wall.
The ball rolls under the bed.
The dog sleeps under the table.

items.p: Ich stelle die Vase neben ___ Fenster.
items.en: I put the vase next to the window.
The vase is next to the window.

groups.subtitle: Two-way prepositions

groups.name: Adjektivendungen nach der/die/das
groups.intro: After the definite article (der/die/das, den, dem), adjectives take the weak endings -e or -en. The ending is -e in the nominative singular and accusative neuter/feminine, and -en everywhere else.

items.p: Der alt___ Mann liest eine Zeitung.
items.en: The old man is reading a newspaper.
The young woman works here.

items.p: Das klein___ Kind spielt im Garten.
items.en: The small child is playing in the garden.
I see the old man.
We help the young woman.
I know the small child.
The new neighbours are friendly.
The big dog barks loudly.

items.p: Ich spreche mit dem nett___ Lehrer.
items.en: I am talking to the nice teacher.
The red car belongs to me.

groups.subtitle: Adjective endings after der/die/das

groups.name: Adjektivendungen nach ein/kein/mein
groups.intro: After ein/eine/kein/mein the adjective takes the strong ending where the article has no ending (masc. nom. -er, fem. nom. -e, neut. nom./acc. -es, masc. acc. -en) and -en in the dative and plural.

items.en: An old man is sitting there.
A young woman comes in.
A small child is crying.
I have a new computer.
That is my new bicycle.
I love my little sister.
He has no old shoes.
That is a beautiful city.

items.p: Wir wohnen in einer groß___ Wohnung.
items.en: We live in a large flat.
I am drinking a cold beer.

groups.subtitle: Adjective endings after ein/kein/mein

groups.name: Präteritum
groups.intro: The Präteritum is the simple past, common in writing. Learn the forms of sein (war), haben (hatte), and the modal and strong verbs: ging, kam, sah, konnte, musste.

items.en: Yesterday I was very tired.
He had no time.
We went to the cinema.
She arrived at eight o'clock.
items.note: Präteritum of kommen: sie kam; separable an- goes to the end.

items.en: I saw an old friend.
He could not come.
I had to get up early.
You were not there yesterday.
They had a lot of fun.
It rained all night.
items.note: Regular verbs add -te: regnen becomes regnete.

groups.subtitle: The simple past

groups.name: Nebensätze mit dass / weil / wenn
groups.intro: After the conjunctions dass, weil, wenn (and ob), the conjugated verb moves to the end of the clause.

items.en: I know that he is coming today.
items.note: After dass the verb goes to the end.

items.p: Ich bleibe zu Hause, weil ich krank ___.
items.en: I am staying home because I am sick.
items.note: After weil the verb goes to the end.

items.p: Wenn es morgen ___, bleiben wir zu Hause.
items.en: If it rains tomorrow, we will stay home.
items.note: In the wenn-clause the verb goes to the end.

items.p: Er sagt, dass er keine Zeit ___.
items.en: He says that he has no time.
items.note: After dass the verb goes to the end.

items.p: Wir gehen nicht, weil das Wetter schlecht ___.
items.en: We are not going because the weather is bad.
items.note: After weil the verb goes to the end.

items.en: I am glad that you are coming.
items.note: After dass the verb goes to the end.

items.p: Sie lernt Deutsch, weil sie in Berlin ___.
items.en: She is learning German because she works in Berlin.
items.note: After weil the verb goes to the end.

items.p: Wenn ich Zeit ___, besuche ich dich.
items.en: If I have time, I will visit you.
items.note: In the wenn-clause the verb goes to the end.

items.en: He believes that she is right.
items.note: After dass the verb goes to the end.

items.en: I do not know whether he is coming.
items.note: After ob the verb also goes to the end.

groups.subtitle: Subordinate clauses

groups.name: Komparativ und Superlativ
groups.intro: The comparative adds -er (schnell → schneller), the superlative uses am -sten or the + -ste. Learn the irregulars gern/lieber/am liebsten and gut/besser/am besten.

items.p: Ich trinke gern Kaffee, aber Tee trinke ich ___.
items.en: I like coffee, but I like tea better.
I like water best of all.
items.note: Superlative of gern is am liebsten.

items.p: Das Wetter ist heute ___ als gestern.
items.en: The weather is better today than yesterday.
He runs faster than I do.

items.p: Das ist das ___ Buch, das ich kenne.
items.en: That is the best book I know.
My brother is taller than I am.
She speaks German better than I do.

items.p: Ich fahre gern Fahrrad, aber ich schwimme ___.
items.en: I like cycling, but I prefer swimming.

items.p: Das ist der ___ Tag meines Lebens.
items.en: That is the most beautiful day of my life.

items.p: Dieses Buch ist ___ als das andere.
items.en: This book is more interesting than the other one.

groups.subtitle: Comparative & superlative

groups.name: Reflexive Verben (Akkusativ)
groups.intro: Reflexive verbs use a pronoun that refers back to the subject: mich, dich, sich, uns, euch, sich. Common ones: sich freuen, sich interessieren, sich treffen, sich beeilen, sich waschen, sich erinnern.

items.en: I am happy about the gift.
items.note: Accusative reflexive for ich is mich.

items.en: He is interested in sports.
items.note: Third person singular reflexive is sich.

items.en: We are meeting at eight o'clock.
items.note: Accusative reflexive for wir is uns.

items.en: Are you hurrying?
items.note: Accusative reflexive for du is dich.

items.p: Die Kinder freuen ___ auf den Ausflug.
items.en: The children are looking forward to the trip.
items.note: Third person plural reflexive is sich.

items.en: I still have to shower.
items.note: Accusative reflexive for ich is mich.

items.en: Please sit down!
items.note: Accusative reflexive for ihr is euch.

items.en: She washes her hands.
items.note: Third person singular reflexive is sich.

items.en: He remembers the appointment.
items.note: Third person singular reflexive is sich.

items.en: We are looking forward to the holiday.
items.note: Accusative reflexive for wir is uns.

groups.subtitle: Reflexive verbs

groups.name: Konjunktiv II: hätte, wäre, würde
groups.intro: Konjunktiv II expresses polite requests and unreal conditions. Common forms: hätte (haben), wäre (sein), würde + infinitive (for most other verbs).

items.p: Wenn ich Zeit ___, würde ich kommen.
items.en: If I had time, I would come.
items.note: Konjunktiv II of haben: ich hätte.

items.en: I would like an ice cream.
It would be nice if you came along.
items.note: Konjunktiv II of sein: es wäre.

items.p: Wenn ich reich ___, würde ich reisen.
items.en: If I were rich, I would travel.
I would gladly help you.
Would you please help me?

items.p: Wenn wir mehr Zeit ___, würden wir länger bleiben.
items.en: If we had more time, we would stay longer.
items.note: Konjunktiv II of haben: wir hätten.

items.en: I would not do that.
I would like to go to Italy.

items.p: Es ___ besser, wenn du früher kommst.
items.en: It would be better if you came earlier.
items.note: Konjunktiv II of sein: es wäre.

groups.subtitle: Konjunktiv II basics

groups.name: Relativsätze
groups.intro: Relative clauses are introduced by a relative pronoun (der, die, das, den, dem …) that agrees with the noun it refers to. The conjugated verb goes to the end of the clause.

items.p: Der Mann, ___ hier wohnt, ist Arzt.
items.en: The man who lives here is a doctor.
items.note: Nominative masculine relative pronoun is der.

items.p: Die Frau, ___ ich kenne, heißt Anna.
items.en: The woman whom I know is called Anna.
items.note: Accusative feminine relative pronoun is die.

items.p: Das Buch, ___ ich lese, ist spannend.
items.en: The book that I am reading is exciting.
items.note: Accusative neuter relative pronoun is das.

items.p: Der Film, ___ wir gestern gesehen haben, war toll.
items.en: The film that we saw yesterday was great.
items.note: Accusative masculine relative pronoun is den.

items.p: Die Kinder, ___ im Garten spielen, sind meine Nachbarn.
items.en: The children who are playing in the garden are my neighbours.
items.note: Nominative plural relative pronoun is die.

items.p: Das Haus, ___ wir gekauft haben, ist alt.
items.en: The house that we bought is old.
items.note: Accusative neuter relative pronoun is das.

items.p: Der Freund, ___ ich vertraue, hilft mir oft.
items.en: The friend whom I trust often helps me.

items.p: Die Stadt, ___ ich besuche, ist schön.
items.en: The city that I am visiting is beautiful.
items.note: Accusative feminine relative pronoun is die.

items.p: Das Mädchen, ___ dort steht, ist meine Schwester.
items.en: The girl standing there is my sister.
items.note: Nominative neuter relative pronoun is das.

items.p: Der Lehrer, ___ uns unterrichtet, ist nett.
items.en: The teacher who teaches us is nice.
items.note: Nominative masculine relative pronoun is der.

groups.subtitle: Relative clauses

groups.name: Genitiv: des / der
groups.intro: The genitive shows possession. Masculine and neuter nouns take des + -s (des Mannes), feminine and plural take der (der Frau, der Kinder).

items.en: That is the man's car.
items.note: Masculine genitive is des + -s on the noun.

items.en: The colour of the wall is beautiful.
The end of the film was sad.
The child's mother is here.
That is the family's house.
The door of the room is open.
The woman's name is Müller.
That is the teacher's bag.
The neighbours' children are loud.

items.p: Wegen ___ Regens bleiben wir zu Hause.
items.en: Because of the rain we are staying home.
items.note: wegen takes the genitive: des Regens.

groups.subtitle: The genitive case
